summary: The PREP Act establishes a dedicated Office of Prison Education within the Bureau of Prisons and creates the Federal Prison Education Program to provide quality education, workforce training, and related support services to incarcerated individuals in federal facilities. The bill also sets up a national clearinghouse for prison education best practices, provides technical assistance to state correctional systems, and mandates specific outreach, counseling, and assistance for incarcerated veterans regarding their educational benefits.

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to expanded educational programs, adult literacy, high school diploma courses, postsecondary education, workforce training, apprenticeships, career counseling, and transition services.
affected_groups.group: Incarcerated individuals in Federal correctional facilities

affected_groups.effect: Receive targeted outreach regarding educational benefits, assistance connecting to approved programs, financial aid counseling, and post-release resource guides, though they are restricted from receiving monthly housing or subsistence stipends while incarcerated.
affected_groups.group: Incarcerated veterans in Federal and State correctional facilities

affected_groups.effect: Have the opportunity to partner with federal correctional facilities to deliver educational programs, submit annual reports, and receive technical assistance.
affected_groups.group: Eligible education providers (colleges, community organizations, employers, etc.)

affected_groups.effect: May receive training, technical assistance, and research resources from the new federal office to help improve their own prison education programs.

key_provisions: Establishes an Office of Prison Education within the Bureau of Prisons headed by a newly appointed Assistant Director for Prison Education.

Creates the Federal Prison Education Program to partner with eligible education providers (such as higher education institutions, local agencies, and community organizations) to deliver academic and vocational training in federal prisons.

Requires participating education providers to prioritize workforce programs in in-demand fields where individuals with felony convictions are legally permitted to work, and to inform students of licensing barriers.

Sets federal matching fund limits at a maximum of 75 percent of the total cost for academic programs and allocates $170,000,000 from Bureau of Prisons appropriations for fiscal years 2027 through 2033.

Requires the Assistant Director, in coordination with other federal agencies and external evaluators, to conduct comprehensive evaluations of student outcomes—including recidivism, employment, and facility safety—over 3-year and 5-year post-release periods.
Establishes a public-facing research and best-practices clearinghouse on the Bureau of Prisons website and provides training and technical assistance to state correctional institutions.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to coordinate outreach, educational assistance connection, financial aid counseling, and resource guides for incarcerated veterans in both federal and state facilities, while restricting certain monthly housing and subsistence stipends during incarceration.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The PREP Act establishes a dedicated Office of Prison Education within the Bureau of Prisons and creates the Federal Prison Education Program to provide quality education, workforce training, and related support services to incarcerated individuals in federal facilities. The bill also sets up a national clearinghouse for prison education best practices, provides technical assistance to state correctional systems, and mandates specific outreach, counseling, and assistance for incarcerated veterans regarding their educational benefits.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a permanent, nationwide federal framework dedicated to coordinating, funding, and evaluating prison education across all federal correctional institutions, backed by $170 million in funding from fiscal years 2027 through 2033. It systematically links correctional education with external providers, workforce readiness, and veteran-specific educational benefits while tracking long-term post-release outcomes.
